content:
The leaf shows scattered whitish-gray powdery patches distributed across the upper surface. The spots are irregular, pale, and appear as a dusty or mealy coating rather than necrotic lesions or dark discoloration. The leaf remains largely green with no tip dieback, no dark sooty coating, and no sunken brown lesions.

This pattern — white to grayish powdery spots covering the leaf surface — is characteristic of Powdery Mildew (fungal mycelium and spores on the leaf surface).
